DR is just damage mitigation for Scholar with Iron Form. Healing is damage mitigation plus damage output with Energy Form. It's a no brainer what I'm choosing every time, especially when both ways can keep Scholar at around full health.  
Every time? I'm not disagreeing with you - I'm disagreeing with the absolute in your statement.  Healing and Damage are not always the best choice.  If you're dealing with damage from multiple sources, even Scholar's healing can't keep up.  Case in point: the game going on at this very moment against Advanced Challenge Infinitor.  Those manifestations will be dealing upwards of 20 or 30 damage next turn - There's not enough healing in the world to keep Scholar safe long.

Scholar has nothing in play and is down to single digit HP on turn 2. There wasn't anything that was saving anybody in that game regardless of what was played. You make it sound like a 3 Iron Form Scholar was a champion where LEE would have failed. Nothing is saving that game from a loss. I don't see what this proves.

Rather than having a single label on each hero, I would actually like a spreadsheet listing capabilities. How many consumable cards (one-shots, powers that self-destruct after use, etc.) destroy environment cards? How many reusable ones? Same 2 things for helping others draw, self draw, ongoing destruction, AoE heal, self heal, cards that deal single-target damage, AoE damage, various forms of DR, an assortment of ways of modeling damage output, a miscellaneous “cards not easily categorized,” and some other info. It would not focus on tricks or combos, though some of the damage models could include boosts and reduction.

I believe that this quantification would be useful for most hereos, at least. Even Nightmist and AA could be at least partially quantified, but Guise would largely be a blob of not easily categorized.

posts.name: Donner
posts.cooked:
I would go for a few things:

1.  Hero difficulty - Tough heroes can be a real problem for beginners

2.  A few sentences describing what that character's gameplay is like

3.  Thematically who the character is similar to.

 

The first option filters gameplay difficulty and the second and third options give the players an overview of the character without overwhelming them in details.  A huge spreadsheet might do the opposite!

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
I generally give new players a choice between Haka (“A Maori brawler”), Ra (Indiana Jones turned into the sun god, aka kill it with fire), Tachyon (female Flash), the Wraith (female Batman), Legacy (Superman), and sometimes Chrono-Ranger (time traveling cowboy).

That’s usually enough to give the player a good selection of easy heroes with strong and familiar flavor. Of course, not all new players are the same. I had one player who’s first hero was Argent Adept, and he did fine.

And of course, that’s just for the first game. After that it really depends on the player.
